description:
The enum-level `#[non_exhaustive]` on `Error` (lib.rs:353) admits new
*variants* in minor releases, but does NOT protect fields inside
existing struct variants. `Error::MalformedAnchor { index, source }`
(lib.rs:397-402) is the only struct-variant in `Error`, and it lacks
its own `#[non_exhaustive]` attribute.

Concrete consequence: a future minor release that wants to surface
additional diagnostic context — e.g., the offending certificate's
serial number, subject DN, or the raw DER bytes — cannot do so
non-breakingly. Every caller pattern-matching the variant with full
field destructuring breaks at compile time:

```rust
// Caller code that currently compiles:
match err {
    Error::MalformedAnchor { index, source } => log(index, source),
    _ => /* enum-level non_exhaustive covered by `_` */,
}
```

After adding a third field, that match must become
`{ index, source, .. }` — a breaking change for every consumer.

This is inconsistent with the rest of the public surface:
- `IoFailure` (lib.rs:223) is `#[non_exhaustive]` and its doc
  explicitly promises 'future minor releases may surface additional
  context'.
- `TrustAnchor` in pkix-path is `#[non_exhaustive]` (pkix-path/src/lib.rs:650)
  with the same promise.
- The `Error` enum itself is `#[non_exhaustive]`.

The fix is one line: add `#[non_exhaustive]` to the variant declaration.
Per-variant `#[non_exhaustive]` is stable since Rust 1.40, well within
the workspace MSRV of 1.73.

```rust
#[non_exhaustive]
MalformedAnchor {
    index: usize,
    source: DerError,
},
```

Internal call site in lib.rs:579-585 already uses functional update via
the struct-literal syntax; that pattern remains legal inside the
defining crate. The tests at lib.rs:740-744 use full destructuring and
would need `.. }` added, which is a single-character change.

Pre-1.0 this is a free fix; post-1.0 it becomes a 'we can't grow the
diagnostic surface without a major bump' problem. File now while
breaking changes are still free per workspace policy (AGENTS.md
'Project phase and decision framing': breaking changes are the
mechanism for getting the design right).

Engineering basis: structural forward-compat consistency. Not opinion.
title: Error::MalformedAnchor struct variant lacks #[non_exhaustive], blocking non-breaking field additions
